theme: The crucifixion, “It is finished”; the burial
readingInstruction: Read John 19:17-42. Jesus is crucified, speaks his last words in John’s Gospel, dies, and is buried. Read slowly. Notice how many Scriptures John says are fulfilled, and the cry “It is finished.”
settingTheScene: Jesus carries his cross to Golgotha, the place of a skull. John, who was there, tells the story with simplicity and attention to detail. He alone records the conversation with his mother, the cry “I thirst,” the word “It is finished,” and the water and blood from his side. John presents the crucifixion not as defeat but as the hour of glory, the completion of the work the Father gave him.
observation: “Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews” (19:19).
“They divided my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots” (19:24).
“And he bowed his head and gave up his spirit” (19:30).
“But one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once there came out blood and water” (19:34).
“Nicodemus, who earlier had come to Jesus by night, also came, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds in weight” (19:39).
interpretation:
Pilate writes a sign for the cross: “Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews,” in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek. The chief priests object, but Pilate says, “What I have written I have written.” Without knowing it, Pilate proclaims the truth to the world in three languages.

The soldiers divide his clothes into four parts and cast lots for the seamless tunic, fulfilling Psalm 22:18. John notes that nothing happens by accident. Near the cross stand his mother, her sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene. Jesus sees his mother and the disciple whom he loved, and says, “Woman, behold, your son!” and “Behold, your mother!” Even in agony, he provides for his mother.

Then, “knowing that all was now finished,” he says, “I thirst.” Psalm 69:21 is fulfilled. They put a sponge of sour wine on a hyssop branch. Hyssop was used at the Passover to put the blood on the doorposts. Then he says, “It is finished,” and bows his head and gives up his spirit. The word is tetelestai, a word used for a paid debt. Jesus did not die as a helpless victim but as someone who completed the work of redemption: the debt paid, the sacrifice offered, the law fulfilled, the Father’s will done. He gave up his spirit; it was not taken from him.

To make sure the bodies do not remain on the crosses on the Sabbath, the soldiers break the legs of the other two men. But when they come to Jesus, they find that he is already dead, and instead a soldier pierces his side with a spear. Blood and water flow out. John emphasizes that he saw it and testifies to it. Not a bone is broken, fulfilling the Passover regulations about the lamb, and they will look on the one they have pierced (Zechariah 12:10). Jesus is the Passover Lamb.

Joseph of Arimathea, a secret disciple, and Nicodemus, who first came by night, step forward in the open. Nicodemus brings a hundred pounds of spices, a royal burial. They wrap the body and lay it in a new tomb in a garden, where no one had yet been laid. Two men who had been afraid now publicly honor Jesus. Death has done its worst. The scene is set for Sunday.
connection: Psalm 22 describes the crucifixion with striking accuracy, and verses 16 to 18 are quoted here. Psalm 69:21 is the vinegar. Exodus 12:22 and 12:46 relate to hyssop and the unbroken bones. Zechariah 12:10 is the pierced one. Isaiah 53:9 says he was with a rich man in his death. Leviticus 16 and Hebrews 9:11-14 explain the sacrifice of atonement. Romans 3:23-26 and Colossians 2:13-14 say the debt of our sin was nailed to the cross. 1 John 5:6-8 speaks of water and blood.
application:
Spend time in silence with “It is finished.” What debt do you still try to pay on your own?

Look at Joseph and Nicodemus: are you hiding your faith? Ask for courage to be open.

Thank Jesus for caring for his mother even in agony. Whom can you care for today?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for saying, “It is finished,” and paying your debt in full.
Tell him what it means to rest in that.
Thank him for his care even in his dying.
